subject: general
question: A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. A sits third to the right of G. C sits second to the right of D. G is not an immediate neighbour of C. E sits to the immediate left of B. How many people sit between D and B when counted from the left of D?
solution:
Given: A, B, C, D, E, F and G are sitting around a circular table facing the centre.

1) A sits third to the right of G. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/003fbbe08253cbea8b08999417ca2fbe79143db75ece2809184c01efa50c7168.png] 

2) C sits second to the right of D.

3) G is not an immediate neighbour of C.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/648b6d9e5ce1019017f8a33d3abef862b0c185ab04d98387df48f59cc3b78053.png] 

4) E sits to the immediate left of B.

After positioning E and B only one position is left which will be occupied by the only person left i.e. F.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e96792086e5c972cf45b9954a66d5f0ce5b59b3ca7d6e769b112be0567dd74e6.png] 

Thus, two people sit between D and B when counted from the left of D.

Hence, "Option 2" is the correct answer.
